title: decision-result v1
description: WHAT ONE DECISIONS OPERATION GIVES BACK when it could say what happened (decisions/Operations.ps1): the value of a known answer in core/Tristate.ps1's sense. The three states of that answer mean, here: KNOWN - this object, whose outcome says the request was done, was replayed from an earlier record of the same id, or was refused with every reason; ABSENT - the store was read and there is no question of that number; UNKNOWN - the store, or the one record asked about, could not be read, with the reason. A refusal is a known fact, not an unknown: the caller is told exactly why nothing was written. EVERY result names the records that could not be read (unreadable) and the readable ones that did not apply (ignored), so a damaged record is never silently skipped by a caller that shows this. Plain data, checked against this schema before it is returned, so the command line, a window and a link between machines all receive one shape.

operation.description: The operation that was asked for.

outcome.description: done: it happened (a read was made, or one record was written). replayed: the same id with the same request was recorded before; this is that record's result and nothing was written. refused: nothing was written; findings says why.

reason.description: One line saying why a request was refused. Empty otherwise.

findings.description: Every rule a refused request broke, one per item. A finding names the field, and never repeats a value that looked like a secret.

sequence.description: The sequence number of the record a write made, or that a replay was answered from.

attempts.description: How many times a write tried to take a sequence number. More than 1 means another writer took one first and this request was checked again against the list as that writer left it.

number.description: The permanent number of the question the operation was about.

questions.description: The questions a list asked for, in number order.

counts.description: How many questions are in each state, by state name, whatever the list was filtered to.

messages.description: What an inbox hands back: what others said that the reader had not read, under every question, oldest first.

upTo.description: For an inbox: the sequence number of the last message handed back, or 0 when there is none; a caller that then marks names this. For a marking: the record it marked up to.

marked.description: For a marking only: how many messages it marked as read. 0 when the reader had already read that far, in which case nothing was written.

authorizations.description: For authorized only, when it is done: for each part asked about (one entry, with no part, for a question without parts), the founder's standing answer that was proven, at the time of asking, signed by his trusted passkey, with no later answer of his in the relay journal, and read as a plain yes.

sequence.description: The record that holds the answer.

signedBy.description: The key id of the passkey that signed it, trusted on this machine at the time of asking.

signedAt.description: When the passkey signed it: the envelope's own signed time, in milliseconds since 1970 UTC.

wordingVersion.description: The wording he answered, which is the wording the question has now.

part.description: The part this authorizes. The record may answer the whole question, which stands for every part he has not answered since.

kinds.description: The table of question kinds, as the kinds operation gives it: by kind name, each with label (how a list names it), means (one sentence) and list (which list of a question it needs: options, parts, or none). It is decisions/question-kinds.json's table, handed out here so that no caller needs the file.

unreadable.description: Records that could not be read: torn, not this schema, of a known kind with data that is not that kind's, missing from the order (a gap of several records is one entry, under its first number), or open in another process. The list is still worked out from every other record.

ignored.description: Records that were read and did not apply, such as a change to a question whose own record is unreadable.

notUnderstood.description: Records whose envelope is well formed and whose kind this version does not know: a later version wrote them. One entry for each kind. They are not damage and are never in unreadable: they are set aside, change nothing this version shows, and cost no question number (decisions/Rules.ps1, the compatibility contract).

strays.description: Files in the store folder that are named like a record and are not one: too far past the end of the order (decisions/Store.ps1 has the limit and why), or a number not written in ten digits; or a link named like a writer's temporary file, which is never followed and never removed. They are not read, not counted and not part of the order; they are named here so that nobody has to find them.

laterKind.description: The records of ONE kind this version does not know: one entry for the kind, however many records it has.

kind.description: The kind's name, as the records give it.

count.description: How many records of that kind the store holds.

first.description: The sequence number of the first of them.

last.description: The sequence number of the last of them. Records of other kinds may lie between the two.

file.description: The record's file name in the store folder.
The file's name in the store folder.

message.description: One thing said under a question. What the record holds: sequence, at, speaker, route, recordedBy, text, wordingVersion. What is worked out from the order of the records each time, and stored nowhere: saidToEarlierWording, arrivedAfterClosing, unreadBy.

sequence.description: The record the words are in. A thread is in this order.

speakerShown.description: How the speaker is named to a person.

routeShown.description: The route in words, the same words everywhere: 'recorded by the warchief from chat' for words another hand wrote down.

recordedBy.description: The role that made the request. For words recorded from chat it is not the speaker.

holdsDirectionOrInvisibleCharacters.description: True when the words hold a direction mark, an embedding, an override, an isolate, a joiner or another character that is not seen. They are stored exactly as typed; a way of showing them isolates the message so that it cannot reorder what is beside it. Worked out from the text each time, stored nowhere.

wordingStated.description: Whether the speaker said which wording of the question they were looking at. When false, a way of showing says 'wording not stated'.

wordingVersion.description: The wording the speaker was looking at; 0 when it was not stated, which is never a wording.

saidToEarlierWording.description: True when the question had already left that wording WHEN THE WORDS WERE SAID: they answered something the question no longer said. Judged at the record's place in the order, and only ever for a STATED wording; never against the wording now: a rewording made afterwards does not flag words said before it.

arrivedAfterClosing.description: True when the question was closed when the words were recorded. They are kept, and reopen nothing.

unreadBy.description: The roles with an inbox, other than the speaker, that have not read up to this record.

asks.description: False for the keeper's words that ask the founder nothing (a note); true otherwise, and for every record that does not say.

act.description: park or unpark when the founder's words record that act of his; empty otherwise.

replaces.description: True when the same speaker's own words were the last said under the question before these (acts left aside): these replace them. Worked out at the record's place.

evidence.description: For words answered on the founder's phone: the SHA-256, in lower-case hex, of the relay journal record that proved them; empty for every other message, and for a stored phone record that holds none.

part.description: The letter of the one part of the question these words answer; empty for words said to the whole question.

partWords.description: That part's words as they read when the answer was recorded; empty when no part is named, or the part was no longer in the question.

signedBy.description: For words answered on the founder's phone: the key id of the passkey the relay channel verified them against, as the record holds it; empty for every other message, and for a record that names none. What the record says, not a verdict: whether that passkey is trusted now is relay's to answer.

number.description: The question the words were said under.

title.description: That question, in its plain words, as it reads now.

count.description: How many messages of the thread, said by others, this reader has not read.

thread.description: The small conversation under one question. All of it is derived from the records. A list carries the counts; one question shown carries the messages too.

count.description: How many messages the thread has.

turn.description: Whose turn it is: the person asked until he speaks, then the other speaker until it replies; 'nobody' while the question is closed. Never stored.

turnShown.description: That, as a person is told it.

unread.description: For each role that has an inbox: how many of these messages it has not read.

messages.description: The messages, in store order. Present when one question is shown.

parts.description: For a question of parts that are answered one by one: each part's letter, and whether the founder has answered it. Absent for any other question.

answered.description: Whether a record answers this part. Never stored: worked out from the order of the records.

followsUp.description: The earlier question a follow-up follows, as context: worked out from the list at the moment of showing, never stored with the new question.

state.description: The earlier question's state; unreadable or absent when the list cannot show it, and then nothing else is said of it.

answer.description: What the founder answered under it, as one text; empty when he did not.

answerCut.description: True when the answer is longer than is carried here: the whole of it is under the earlier question's own number.

outcome.description: What it was closed with; empty while it is open.

note.description: What the record did to the question, in a few words.

view.description: One question as it stands now: its words (schema/decision-question.v1, every field present) and what the records say has happened to it.

number.description: Permanent: given once, never changed, never given to another question.

state.description: open or closed today. The list of states is in decisions/Rules.ps1 and grows there; a reader shows a state it does not know by its name.

wordingVersion.description: 1 when added, and one more for every change to the title, whatItIs, yesMeans, options or parts: the fields a person reads before answering.

outcome.description: What was done, when the question is closed. Empty while it is open.

reopenReason.description: Why it was last reopened. Empty if it never was.

updatedAt.description: When the latest record that changed this question was written. Words said under it do not change it.

history.description: Every record that applied to this question, in order.

importance.description: How much the task the question belongs to matters overall: a label of decisions/Rules.ps1's importances, normal for a question that was given none.

importanceShown.description: That, in the few plain words shown beside the question; empty for the default.

blocks.description: How much of that task's work stands still until the question is answered: a label of decisions/Rules.ps1's blockings, part for a question that was given none.

blocksShown.description: That, in the few plain words shown beside the question; empty for the default.

needsPasskey.description: Present, and true, only for a question its asker marked as needing a passkey: from the phone it is answered only with a fresh passkey. Absent for every other question.
